stat: Share of the UK creative industries' 2023 GVA that sits within its highest-AI-adoption sub-sector (IT, software and computer services)
unit: percent (£49.1bn of £124bn total creative industries GVA)
method: Recipe B (sector cut) — cross-referencing a DCMS monetary dataset (GVA by sub-sector) against a DSIT behavioural dataset (AI adoption rate by sub-sector) to produce a derived observation neither source publishes alone

sources_used.title: DCMS Economic Estimates: GVA 2023 (provisional)
sources_used.publisher: Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS)

sources_used.title: AI Adoption Plan: Creative Industries
sources_used.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)

workings: IT, software and computer services GVA (2023): £49.1bn. Total UK creative industries GVA (2023): £124bn. £49.1bn / £124bn = 0.396, rounded to 'nearly 40%'. Separately, the AI Adoption Plan for the Creative Industries (DSIT, June 2026) reports 60% AI adoption for the same IT/software/computer-services sub-sector, the highest of any creative-industries sub-sector measured (vs 53% design, 44% film/TV, 22% music/performing arts). The two figures are not contemporaneous (2023 GVA vs 2026 adoption); presented as a directional/structural observation about where AI adoption concentrates by economic value, not a causal claim.
